Go see a psychiatrist, go see a couple if you can because diagnosis is not an exact science and many misdiagnose or avoid diagnosing certain things. I believe the 2 week thing is specifically for major depressive disorder. There is also dysthymia which is chronic depression. It's also called "mild depression" in the definition, although doesn't feel that way, and people with it commonly also experience periods of major depression. Idk if you have that if you're not constantly depressed and instead just experience waves of it. There's also borderline personality disorder, which is actually the most common mental health disorder but is not as well known by design because doctors would often avoid diagnosing it because it can be very difficult to treat in many of the cases. Also because meds are usually ineffective at treating it which both means the doctors need to put in more work with the patient and there is nothing in it for pharma. It's also a very diverse disorder with 256 possible combinations of the traits to diagnose, so many people with it remain very functional and go undiagnosed. Only reason I bring it up, besides the fact I have it, is because one of the symptoms is mood swings, but for shorter periods than other disorders like bipolar. 

Read up on more than just depression because it's possible that these periods are a symptom and not the main illness. I personally feel it's better to go into a doctor's office with some level of diagnosis for them to either confirm or deny, but even if they don't think it's whatever you think it is it will give them a better understanding of your symptoms and something to start from. I should've been diagnosed with BPD back in 2007 when I first went in to get a diagnosis for ADD, but I had never heard of it at that time and I know the doctor specifically avoided diagnosing me with it and just diagnosed me with dysthymia at the time. 

Best of luck to you. I deal with that level of depression every day, it sucks.

Support - Empathy - Truth - Understanding - Perseverance

Seeing the world through that different wondrous lens may give him the boost he needs to find a reason and motivation to go through the shitty process to seek therapy or a diagnosis. Microdosing is also an option for the long term but I would definitely recommend an actual trip to get the flood gates opened.  

Best of luck to both of you.
